_comment: KV cache is modelled as two terms: kvElementsPerToken * context + kvElementsFixed. That single formula covers both architectures here. Qwen 3.5/3.8 are hybrid attention/SSM: only 1 layer in 4 holds a KV cache and the SSM layers have fixed-size state, so the fixed term is 0 and folded into overhead. Gemma 4 uses sliding-window attention: the few full-attention layers scale with context, while the sliding-window layers are capped at the window and never grow. Every number below is derived from the GGUF header; the detail block records where it came from.

qwen35-9b.name: Qwen 3.5 9B Q6_K
qwen35-9b._maxTokensComment: Published: 'Adequate Output Length: 32,768 tokens for most queries'. This is a ceiling, not the value a harness is handed - harness.maxOutputPercent in server.json takes a share of whatever context was actually loaded and this caps it, so at 32K the harness still sees 8192.

detail.derivation: 8 attention layers x 4 kv heads x (256+256) = 16384 per token. The other 24 layers are SSM with fixed-size state.

geometry.summary: hybrid attention/SSM: 8 of 32 layers hold a KV cache

overhead._comment: Measured through serve.ps1 at 64K and 256K, vision on and off. The implied overhead is identical at both context lengths, which confirms the KV coefficient. It is negative because the GGUF file is larger than what ends up resident: metadata and tokenizer tables are counted in the file size but never reach VRAM.

sampling._comment: From the Qwen 3.5 documentation, which is the only model here that publishes a profile for coding specifically. Switch by changing 'profile'; every value is sent to llama-server explicitly, because its own defaults (temp 0.80, top_k 40, min_p 0.05) match none of these and can change between releases.

coding._comment: Documented as 'thinking mode, precise coding tasks'. The launcher ships this one because a coding agent is what it exists to feed.

thinking._comment: Documented as 'thinking mode, general tasks'. Note that this model is in the 0.8B-9B range where the docs say reasoning is off by default; enable it with --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":true}'.

qwen35-9b.note: Stable. No MTP: the GGUF carries no nextn_predict_layers.

qwen38-27b.name: Qwen 3.8 27B UD-Q3_K_XL
qwen38-27b._maxTokensComment: Not published for this model; taken from Qwen 3.5, which is the same family and generation and states 32,768. A ceiling only, capped further by harness.maxOutputPercent.

mtp._costComment: Measured on CUDA. Embedded MTP builds a draft context against the full model, so it costs far more than a small companion file: 13428 MiB without it, 14628 with, at 64K.

macos._costComment: Measured on a 24 GiB M4 Pro, Metal, with vision at 32K: 15717 MiB without, 16534 with. Cheaper than on CUDA, but do not trust it as a constant: it grows with context, because the draft context carries its own KV cache.
macos._maxContextComment: The longest context this was actually run at, not a derived limit. At 32K with vision it loads and generates. At 48K with vision the same build loads, answers /health with ok, and then dies on the first decode with kIOGPUCommandBufferCallbackErrorOutOfMemory. Because costMiB is modelled as a flat number, the memory check alone would wave 48K through, so this ceiling is what stops it. Raise it only after running the configuration you are raising it for.
macos.note: Measured at 32K: acceptance 0.93, and 10.6 tok/s against 10.7 without it. Enabled so you can confirm that on your own workload.

mtp._macosFindingComment: Measured and it buys nothing on this architecture. At 32K with vision the draft acceptance rate is 0.93 (109 of 117 accepted, mean draft length 3.79) and generation still comes out at 10.6 tok/s against 10.7 without it. Acceptance is not the problem; the speedup simply does not arrive. The likely reason is architectural rather than a tuning failure: this is a hybrid attention/SSM model where 3 layers in 4 hold recurrent state, and an SSM layer has to walk its state forward one position at a time. Verifying 3.79 drafted tokens in a single pass therefore still costs 3.79 sequential state updates, which is exactly the work speculative decoding is supposed to avoid. Treat that as the standing explanation, not as something measured directly. It does not generalise to the Gemma 4 models here, which are pure sliding-window attention with no recurrent state and have not been tested on Metal.
mtp._autoEnableComment: Turned off by choice, and now for two separate reasons. On a 16 GB CUDA card this model already sits near the ceiling: with vision at 64K it needs 14720 MiB and MTP would add 1200 more, leaving about 60 MiB. On Metal it fits at short contexts but delivers no speedup at all; see _macosFindingComment. Set this to true on a CUDA card with room to spare.

detail.derivation: 65 blocks = 64 real layers + 1 nextn (MTP). 64/4 = 16 attention layers x 4 kv heads x (256+256) = 32768 per token. Measured on a 16 GB GPU: with vision at 64K it uses 15.2 GB.

geometry.summary: hybrid attention/SSM: 16 of 65 layers hold a KV cache

overhead._comment: Measured through serve.ps1 at 64K and 128K, vision on and off. Identical overhead at both lengths confirms the KV coefficient. Negative for the same reason as the 9B, plus the blk.64 tensors that llama.cpp skips when MTP is off.

sampling._comment: The Qwen 3.8 page publishes only thinking and instruct; it has no coding profile. The 'coding' one below is the only extrapolated set of numbers in this file and is labelled as such.

coding._comment: EXTRAPOLATED, not published for this model. Qwen 3.5 documents its coding profile as its thinking profile with the temperature dropped to 0.6 and the presence penalty zeroed, leaving top_p and top_k alone; the same adjustment applied to this model's thinking profile gives these numbers. It is also what the launcher sent before sampling moved into config, so keeping it active changes nothing about how the model behaves today. Switch to 'thinking' for the values Qwen actually publishes.

thinking._comment: Published. Reasoning depth is a separate control: --chat-template-kwargs '{"reasoning_effort":"medium"}', where the options are xhigh (the default), medium, low and none.

qwen38-27b.note: Unsloth Q3. MTP layers are embedded in the model file.

qwen36-35b-a3b.name: Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B UD-Q3_K_XL
qwen36-35b-a3b._maxTokensComment: Published: 'Adequate Output Length: 32,768 tokens for most queries'. A ceiling only, capped by harness.maxOutputPercent against the context actually loaded.
qwen36-35b-a3b._imageMinTokensComment: Same 1024 as the other Qwen entries, and not by analogy: this encoder's header is identical to the 27B's, which is the one that value was verified on. Both report clip.vision block_count 27, embedding_length 1152, image_size 768, patch_size 16 and spatial_merge_size 2, so both encode 576 tokens at native resolution and both accept the same floor above it.

cache._comment: Overrides the global cacheType in server.json, per platform, because this model is large enough that the KV type decides whether a long context is reachable at all. Weights are 16064 MiB before the encoder's 858, so on a 24 GiB Mac (Metal recommends 18186) f16 leaves room for roughly 32K and nothing beyond it.

macos._comment: UNMEASURED ON METAL. The collapse that makes quantizing a bad trade was observed on CUDA, where flash attention has no kernel for a quantized KV cache and attention silently moves to the CPU; whether Metal has the same hole nobody here has checked. q8_0 is the mildest option at 1.0625 bytes per element, roughly halving the cache against f16 while staying far from the 4-bit types. If generation looks degraded or prompt processing collapses, set this back to f16 and shorten the context instead - that is the trade this project recommends everywhere else. Verify before trusting it: run once with each and compare tokens per second.

windows._comment: Deliberately NOT quantized, and not an oversight. Measured on CUDA with this build: f16 gives 3355 tok/s prompt and 65.1 generation, q4_1 gives 40 and 10.9 - a gigabyte saved for 84x slower prompt processing, because CUDA flash attention has no quantized-KV kernel and attention falls off the GPU while nothing reports an error. A card big enough for this model is a card big enough for an f16 cache.

detail.derivation: Read from the GGUF header without downloading the weights, by fetching the first 12 MB of the file and parsing the metadata block. 40 blocks / full_attention_interval 4 = 10 attention layers x 2 kv heads x (256+256) = 10240 per token. The other 30 layers are SSM with fixed-size state (ssm.state_size 128, ssm.conv_kernel 4, ssm.group_count 16), so the fixed term is 0 and folded into overhead, the same convention the other two Qwen entries use. Note headCountKv is 2 here against 4 on the 9B and 27B: this model holds half the KV per attention layer, which is why a 35B has a cheaper cache than the 27B.
detail.moe: 256 experts, 8 active per token. All 256 must be resident, so the weights bill is the full 16064 MiB while only about 3B parameters are active per token - the same shape as the Gemma 26B-A4B, and the reason generation is far faster than the parameter count suggests.

geometry.summary: hybrid attention/SSM mixture of experts: 10 of 40 layers hold a KV cache, 8 of 256 experts active

sampling._comment: Published for this model, including a coding profile, which is why nothing here is extrapolated.

coding._comment: Documented as thinking mode with the temperature lowered for precise coding; every other value is the thinking profile unchanged.

qwen36-35b-a3b._mtpComment: MTP exists for this model but cannot be a step-4 toggle, so no mtp block is declared here. Unlike the 27B, which carries its nextn layers inside the same file, and unlike Gemma 4, which ships a small companion draft, Qwen 3.6 publishes MTP as a SEPARATE FULL BUILD in unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-MTP-GGUF: 41 blocks against 40, nextn_predict_layers 1, 753 tensors against 733, and 16429 MiB against 16064 for the same UD-Q3_K_XL quantization. Choosing it means downloading a different 16 GB file, which is a decision at step 2, not step 4. Register it as its own catalog entry if you want it. Temper expectations first: the vendor's own figure for MoE models is 1.15-1.25x against 1.4-2.2x for dense ones, and the 27B measured here - also hybrid attention/SSM - gained nothing at 0.93 draft acceptance.
qwen36-35b-a3b.note: Hybrid attention/SSM mixture of experts. No overhead block: nothing about this model has been measured on any platform yet, so the fit table borrows constants and says so on screen.

gemma4-e4b.name: Gemma 4 E4B QAT
gemma4-e4b._maxTokensComment: Google publishes no output-length recommendation for any Gemma 4 variant, so this is a chosen ceiling rather than a stated one, set to match the Qwen entries. It is safe to leave generous because harness.maxOutputPercent is what actually bounds a reply, against the context that was really loaded.

mtp._costComment: Measured: 4610 MiB without, 4676 with. A 57 MB draft model plus its context.

detail.derivation: Header arithmetic gives 7 full layers x 2 kv heads x (512+512) = 14336 per token, but measurement says 8192, which is exactly 4 layers. shared_kv_layers=18 is the reason: 3 of the 7 full-attention layers reuse another layer's cache. The measured value is used. Fixed term: 35 sliding layers x 2 kv heads x (256+256) x 512 window = 18350080, not adjusted for sharing because it is under 11 MiB either way.
detail.measured: Calibrated on a 16 GB NVIDIA GPU across 64K/128K and vision on/off. The KV delta between 64K and 128K measured 320 MiB against a predicted 560 MiB, which is what exposed the shared-KV layers. With the corrected coefficient the model reproduces all four measurements exactly.

geometry.summary: sliding-window attention: 7 of 42 layers scale with context, 35 capped at a 512-token window

overhead._comment: baseMiB is negative because this is a MatFormer: its per-layer embeddings stay in system RAM instead of VRAM, so roughly 1.2 GB of the file is never resident on the GPU. visionMiB is far below Qwen's 448 because Gemma's encoder is lighter.

sampling._comment: Google's default Gemma 4 parameters, identical across every variant and unchanged by QAT. Note topK 64, against 20 for the Qwen family: sending one number to both families is wrong for one of them.

default._comment: temperature, topP and topK are published. minP, presencePenalty and repeatPenalty are NOT: they are set here to the values that disable them, because llama-server's own minP default is 0.05 and silently inheriting a filter nobody asked for is worse than turning it off on purpose. Thinking is controlled separately with --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}'.

gemma4-e4b.note: Smallest of the family and caps at 128K, unlike its siblings. Verified end to end: 89 tok/s with vision and speculative decoding.

gemma4-12b.name: Gemma 4 12B QAT

mtp._costComment: Measured: 7492 MiB without, 7786 with, at 128K. That is the 242 MB draft model plus 52 MiB of context.

detail.derivation: Scaling term: 8 full layers x 1 kv head x (512+512) = 8192 per token. Fixed term: 40 sliding layers x 8 kv heads x (256+256) x 1024 window = 167772160. The context-scaling layers deliberately use a single kv head, which is why 256K stays cheap.
detail.measured: Calibrated on a 16 GB NVIDIA GPU at 64K, 128K and 256K with vision on and off. The implied overhead came out at exactly 347 MiB at all three context lengths, which confirms the KV coefficient derived from the header needs no correction. shared_kv_layers is 0 on this model.

geometry.summary: sliding-window attention: 8 of 48 layers scale with context, 40 capped at a 1024-token window

overhead._comment: Measured, not assumed. Both numbers are well below Qwen's 256/448: Gemma's compute buffers and vision encoder are lighter.

sampling._comment: Google's default Gemma 4 parameters, identical across every variant and unchanged by QAT. See gemma4-e4b for why minP is pinned rather than left out.

gemma4-12b.note: The dense flagship of the family. Very cheap KV cache for its size.

gemma4-26b-a4b.name: Gemma 4 26B-A4B QAT (MoE)

mtp._costComment: Estimated from the 12B: same 240 MB draft size, so the same shape of cost. Not measured, because MTP never fits on a 16 GB card with this model.

detail.derivation: Scaling term: 5 full layers x 2 kv heads x (512+512) = 10240 per token. Fixed term: 25 sliding layers x 8 kv heads x (256+256) x 1024 window = 104857600. Mixture of experts: 8 of 128 experts run per token, but ALL of them must be resident, so the weights cost is the full 14.25 GB.
detail.measured: Calibrated on a 16 GB NVIDIA GPU at 64K and 128K, with vision on and off. The implied overhead came out at exactly 313 MiB at both context lengths, confirming the KV coefficient from the header. With vision at 64K the whole thing occupies 15644 MiB and does fit on a 16 GB card, with 351 MiB to spare.

geometry.summary: sliding-window attention: 5 of 30 layers scale with context, 25 capped at a 1024-token window

overhead._comment: Measured, not assumed. Being a mixture of experts changes the weights bill, not the compute buffers: these are in line with the dense 12B.

sampling._comment: Google's default Gemma 4 parameters, identical across every variant and unchanged by QAT. See gemma4-e4b for why minP is pinned rather than left out.

gemma4-26b-a4b.note: Mixture of experts: 4B active parameters, but all 128 experts occupy memory.
